title: Can Deep Neural Networks Improve Compression of Very Large Scientific Data?
summary: Replaces traditional predictors in error-bounded compressors such as SZ3.1 with pretrained weather models including GraphCast, Aurora, and CRA5. It adds large-model inference to the compression pipeline and requires suitable domain foundation models. More accurate predictions do not improve the aggregate dataset compression ratio because the residuals' spatial structure hurts entropy coding.
rationale: A useful negative result showing that prediction accuracy does not imply better compression, but the terabyte-scale scientific data and domain models are outside the reader's normal workload.
technique: Weather foundation models as compression predictors

claims.statement: Replaces traditional predictors in error-bounded compressors such as SZ3.1 with pretrained weather models including GraphCast, Aurora, and CRA5. It adds large-model inference to the compression pipeline and requires suitable domain foundation models. More accurate predictions do not improve the aggregate dataset compression ratio because the residuals' spatial structure hurts entropy coding.
Reports up to 91% better reconstruction quality and up to 9.6x higher compression ratios for highly predictable variables, but no dataset-level compression-ratio improvement.
